title: Healthcare needs after post-COVID rehabilitation with interdisciplinary specialized diagnostics: a mixed-methods study
summary:
Rehabilitation plays an important crucial in the care of people affected by post-COVID-19 conditions. Previous studies have shown that rehabilitation programs can improve functional ability, reduce symptoms, and enhance the quality of life for those affected. However, little is still known about the long-term effectiveness of specific rehabilitation measures and what support patients continue to need after completing rehabilitation.
In our study, we are therefore investigating an inpatient complex post-COVID rehabilitation program. We track the participants’ health, symptoms, and participation in daily life and work before, during, and up to one year after the rehabilitation.
We collect quantitative data through standardized questionnaires, clinical assessments, and documentation of rehabilitation services, as well as qualitative data through interviews with participants. The primary outcome of the quantitative analyses is self-reported fatigue twelve months after the end of rehabilitation.
In addition, interviews are conducted to gain a deeper understanding of how participants experience daily life after rehabilitation, what benefits they gain from the program, and where ongoing support is needed. We also analyze which regional support and care services are available, which are actually used, and where gaps in care exist.
The findings are intended to help further develop post-COVID rehabilitation and follow-up care, better coordinate existing support services, and sustainably improve the long-term health, quality of life, and social participation of people affected by post-COVID conditions.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
We include patients aged 18 to 65 years who are diagnosed with COVID-19 disease or SARS-CoV-2 infection and post COVID-19 condition and other pneumological, cardiological, neurological or psychological symptoms referred by the German Pension Insurance North and other pension insurance providers from all over Germany.
Exclusion criteria:
We exclude patients with post-vac syndrome, exclusive or very severe myalgic encephalomyelitis or chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) or monothematic severe pneumological, psychological or neurological symptoms for which an activating rehabilitation is not possible. Further exclusion criteria are significant language problems and a significant impairment of daily life that makes a rehabilitation program impossible.
